headline: High: shared filesystem and broad egress create default risks of prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors between Continue and RD-Agent.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Continue reads workspace files and uses MCP/tool calls; RD-Agent can run browsers and has broad network egress. Their shared filesystem-based state means content produced by one can be consumed by the other, so attacker-controlled text can cross the boundary. This is not proven by direct interaction evidence, but the pathway is plausible in default setups.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace directory, prompt-like content can cross from one to the other.
IF Continue parses RD-Agent-generated files as instructions, injection becomes actionable.
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent.
Disable automatic ingestion of generated files.
Require human review before MCP tool calls.
Use read-only mounts for shared artifacts.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to inter-agent files.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Continue touches source code, open editor buffers, and workspace files; RD-Agent handles logs, execution traces, financial reports, and research datasets, and both have broad network egress. If they share a workspace or credentials, sensitive material can flow from one agent into the other's outputs or external API calls. The pairwise leakage path is credible even though direct coupling is undocumented.
conditions: IF the two agents share a directory containing secrets, logs, or proprietary code, leakage is possible.
IF either agent forwards file contents to a third-party model API, sensitive data can leave the host.
mitigations: Use separate secrets stores.
Mount shared folders read-only.
Block outbound traffic except approved endpoints.
Redact logs and traces before handoff.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention policies.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Continue can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses; RD-Agent also has file access via log/ and broad API use, so both can mutate overlapping local state if co-located. The profiles do not show git locking or explicit coordination, so concurrent writes can clobber artifacts even though RD-Agent's write scope is narrower than Continue's.
conditions: IF both agents write into the same project tree, file clobbering can occur.
IF RD-Agent and Continue run concurrently without locks, race conditions can corrupt shared artifacts.
mitigations: Assign disjoint output directories.
Serialize writes with a lock file.
Disable concurrent runs on the same repo.
Snapshot before each agent run.
requires-engineering: add transactional workspace coordination.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Continue can generate code or edits from workspace context, and RD-Agent can use those outputs in research or automation workflows. Because neither profile shows a verification gate between them, one agent's output can become the other's input with no guaranteed fact-checking. That makes downstream mistakes plausible in default use, though not clearly irreversible.
conditions: IF RD-Agent consumes Continue-produced files as authoritative inputs, errors can cascade.
IF Continue edits are used by RD-Agent without validation, incorrect assumptions propagate.
mitigations: Insert a manual review step between agents.
Require citations for any factual claims passed onward.
Keep generated artifacts separate from source inputs.
Run a diff check before downstream use.
requires-engineering: add schema validation for inter-agent handoffs.

E_compliance.rationale: Continue handles source code, editor buffers, and model-provider API keys; RD-Agent handles financial reports, execution traces, logs, and Kaggle/OpenAI/Azure/DeepSeek APIs. If regulated or sensitive data is placed into RD-Agent's cloud APIs, residency and retention obligations may differ from Continue's local IDE workflow. The profiles do not prove a specific violation, so this is a medium compliance mismatch risk.
conditions: IF EU PII, PHI, or confidential financial data is routed through RD-Agent's external APIs, compliance obligations may be triggered.
IF Continue and RD-Agent are used on the same regulated dataset, retention policies may diverge.
mitigations: Classify data before handoff.
Keep regulated data out of external APIs.
Review vendor DPAs and residency terms.
Disable cloud calls for sensitive projects.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing by data class.
